About Customer.io

Over 9,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data.

About the role

Hi, my name is Diep N, VP, Finance at Customer.io, and I'm looking for a Global Controller to take the close, the books, and our control environment and make them theirs.

We're a global, remote-first, private company built on subscription and usage-based revenue, and as we grow we need a controller who can lead the team already in place and sharpen the fundamentals. You'll lead a team of ~7, growing, across revenue accounting, close, AP/AR, payroll, and treasury, and partner closely with me and, given our CFO's broad remit, with stakeholders across Sales, Legal, IT, HR, and Engineering.

What you'll do

• Lead monthly and quarterly close, GL, AP/AR, payroll, and account reconciliations, delivering accurate, timely US GAAP financials. Close currently runs ~10 business days; get us to 6-8 days within your first 12 months, with fewer post-close adjustments and aged reconciliations.

• Own revenue accounting and serve as our technical accounting authority on subscription and usage-based revenue recognition (ASC 606), including the ARR-to-GAAP bridge: reconciling ARR, billings, deferred revenue, contract assets, and usage true-ups to reported revenue, and explaining the delta to leadership and the board in plain terms.

• Author technical accounting position memos on contract modifications, SSP allocation, variable consideration, and capitalized contract costs, the work that makes "technical accounting authority" real.

• Own equity compensation accounting (ASC 718): grant accuracy, 409A timing, expense, modifications, and cap-table integrity, in partnership with stock plan administration.

• Manage and grow a team of ~7, with room to scale, building trust quickly and developing the leads beneath you.

• Build a control framework suited to a global, remote-first, private company with subscription and usage-based revenue, keeping the books audit-ready.

• Own our accounting systems roadmap and drive automation across close and reporting.

• Own select treasury operations, including cash management and banking relationships, and partner on FX exposure monitoring given our multi-currency footprint.

• Run our external audit relationship and coordinate with external tax partners on compliance, provisions, and filings.

• Manage the realities of a distributed, remote-first global team: statutory accounting coordination, payroll and contractor controls, entity reporting, and working with Legal, HR, and Tax on international compliance.

What we're looking for

• 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including leading a team through managers or leads.

• A Big 4 (or equivalent top-tier public accounting) foundation.

• Deep US GAAP mastery, particular strength in subscription and usage-based revenue recognition (ASC 606).

• A concrete, personally-owned automation or AI deployment in accounting with a measurable result, eliminating a manual reconciliation, reducing close time, or lowering error rate, that you can speak to in detail.

• Experience scaling an accounting function that was already running, not building one from zero.

• A proven track record with external audits and keeping books audit-ready.

• Strong leadership and communication skills, with credibility partnering with senior, cross-functional stakeholders.

• Nice to have: internal controls or SOX-readiness experience; remote-first/globally distributed company experience; M&A or deal accounting exposure; CPA license, active or inactive.

Compensation & Benefits

We believe in transparency. Starting salary for this role ranges from $250k to $280k USD (or equivalent in local currency), structured by geographic zone and depending on experience. In addition to base salary, this role includes an equity grant in the form of stock options, so you share in the success you help build.

Our inclusive benefits package supports your well-being and growth, including 100% coverage of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and supplemental insurance premiums for you and your family. We also offer 16 weeks paid parental leave, unlimited PTO, stipends for remote work and wellness, a professional development budget, and more.

See full benefits here →

Our Process

No gotchas, no trick questions - just a clear, human process designed to help both of us make an informed decision.

• 30-minute recruiter screen

• 45-minute hiring manager screen

• Two 30-minute cross-functional chats: one with a Legal partner, one with a People partner

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Cells Infrastructure team, you'll help build the architecture that lets GitLab.com scale horizontally. Cells splits GitLab.com into independent units, each with its own application and data stack, behind a shared routing layer.

You'll build the services and application changes that make Cells work: the control plane that tracks cells and organizations, the routing logic that sends each request to the right cell, and the changes inside the GitLab application that keep data unique and consistent across cells. Your work will directly support moving customer organizations onto Cells, one of GitLab's most important scaling initiatives.

You'll work across Go, Ruby on Rails, and TypeScript.

What you’ll do

  • Design, build, and maintain the Cells control plane, a Go service using gRPC (remote procedure calls) and backed by Cloud Spanner that tracks cells, organizations, and globally unique resources.
  • Extend the global routing layer, written in TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers, so requests reach the right cell. This includes classifying requests by path, namespace, and token, and supporting more protocols and services.
  • Make changes in the GitLab Rails application so it works across multiple cells: claiming globally unique resources, propagating organization context, and keeping cell-local data consistent.
  • Design application programming interfaces (APIs) and data models with correctness, idempotency, and backward compatibility in mind, so changes can roll out safely across a fleet of cells.
  • Write thorough automated tests, including unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, and improve test coverage and reliability across the services we own.
  • Instrument your services with OpenTelemetry for metrics, logs, and distributed tracing. Help define service level objectives (SLOs) and take part in on-call for the services you build.
  • Work with product teams to make their features cell-compatible, and review their changes for Cells correctness.
  • Write clear design documents, architecture decision records, and documentation, and take part in code review as both author and reviewer.

What you’ll bring

  • Professional experience building and running backend services in production, including monitoring, debugging, and incident response. You've instrumented services with OpenTelemetry and used distributed tracing to debug requests across service boundaries.
  • Proficiency in Go, or strong experience in another backend language and willingness to work in Go daily.
  • Experience with Ruby on Rails and TypeScript, or the willingness to become productive in both. Our control plane is written in Go, the GitLab application in Rails, and our edge routing layer in TypeScript.
  • Experience designing APIs using gRPC or Representational State Transfer (REST), and working with relational or distributed databases, including schema design, transactions, and migrations.
  • A strong understanding of distributed-systems fundamentals, such as consistency, idempotency, concurrency, retries, and failure handling.
  • Solid grounding in engineering best practices: test-driven development, small iterative merge requests, thorough code review, feature flags for safe rollouts, and observable, well-documented code.
  • Experience working effectively in distributed, all-remote teams: you default to asynchronous, written-first communication, document decisions in issues and merge requests, hand off work cleanly across time zones, and stay transparent about progress and blockers.
  • If you've worked with Cloud Spanner, Cloudflare Workers, Kubernetes, multi-tenant or sharded architectures, or contributed to GitLab, that's a plus, not a requirement.

About the team

The Cells Infrastructure team is part of GitLab's Scale & Architecture organization, which builds and operates the core services that let GitLab.com grow. Every team in the organization owns its services end to end, from design through on-call.

Beyond the control plane and routing services you'll help build, we're responsible for:

  • Provisioning cells across Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud.
  • Ring-based deployments that keep the fleet in step with GitLab's release cadence.
  • SLOs, alerting, and on-call for the platform.
  • The infrastructure for moving customer organizations between cells.

Our team mixes Backend Engineers and Site Reliability Engineers who work side by side on the same services. We work closely with delivery, database, migration, and product teams across GitLab. Feature teams own how their services behave on the Cells platform.
